references.text: Parallel text in Deuteronomy that repeats the command not to worship idols and describes God as a jealous God who punishes the sins of fathers on children.
The Lord declares that His name is Jealous, and that He is a jealous God (אֵל קַנָּא), the same expression used in Exodus 20:5.
Describes the Lord your God as a consuming fire, a jealous God, who warns against idolatry.
Repeats that the Lord your God is a jealous God and warns of His wrath when idols are worshipped.
Repeats the principle that God punishes the wrongdoing of fathers on children to the third and fourth generation (עַל־בָּנִים עַל־שִׁלֵּשִׁים וְעַל־רִבֵּעִים).
Describes God's character as one who punishes the wrongdoing of fathers on children and grandchildren to the third and fourth generation.
Confirms that God is faithful and keeps His covenant, but repays those who hate Him by destroying them.
Joshua declares that the Lord is a holy God, a jealous God who will not forgive transgressions.
Describes the Lord as a jealous and avenging God (אֵל קַנּוֹא).
Discusses the principle that children should not bear punishment for their fathers' sins, but each soul shall die for its own sin.
Prophesies about a new covenant where each person will die for their own sin, not their fathers'.
Complementary warning against idolatry confirming the requirement of exclusive worship.
Confirmation of the consequence of generational transmission of idolatry and the Lord's wrath.
